newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl to offer miners compromise package - report.
newsitem.headline: Kohl to offer miners compromise package - report.

text.p: German chancellor Helmut Kohl is to offer miners a compromise on planned cuts to subsidies for the industry when he meets mining leaders in Bonn on Thursday, the Bild mass circulation daily newspaper reported.
The Bild said that Kohl will offer miners some 300 million marks a year in state finances over the next three years to cushion the blow of the subsidy reduction.
The plan is however dependent on the regional government of North Rhine-Westphalia also increasing its support of the industry over the next eight years, the paper added.
Coalminers in pits around Germany's walked out last Friday after Bonn said it would cut subsidies to 3.8 billion marks by 2005 instead of the 6.5 billion marks unions have proposed.

Bonn's government district has been paralysed for three days this week by protests from thousands of miners. Talks with the government were due to take place on Tuesday but were postponed until Thursday by Kohl.
